# Build: Pre-Compilation Validation & Error Recovery

**Purpose:** Final validation gate before `dotnet build`. Scans all generated `Designer.cs`, `.cs`, and `.resx` files, validates against skill-extraction data and WinForms SDK rules, and either clears the build or halts with actionable error messages.

**Input:** All files generated by Stage 5 + `skill-extraction.json` (Stage — Control Skill Extraction)  
**Output:** ✅ BUILD ALLOWED — or — ❌ BUILD BLOCKED with specific halt messages

---

## Validation Workflow (MANDATORY — Execute in Order)

⛔ **Any single FAIL blocks compilation. Do not proceed to `dotnet build` until all checks pass.**

---

### Check 1: Skill-Based API Validation (CRITICAL)

Load `skill-extraction.json`. For every Syncfusion control used in any `Designer.cs` or `.cs` file:

```
FOR EACH Syncfusion control in generated files:

  1. FIND entry in skill-extraction.json → controls[] where control == "<ControlName>"
     ❌ Not found → FAIL: "Control '<ControlName>' not in skill-extraction.json
                           Was this control added after Stage — Control Skill Extraction ran?
                           Fix: re-run Stage — Control Skill Extraction for this control, then rebuild."

  2. VALIDATE using directive in code files matches controls[].using_directive exactly
     ❌ Mismatch → FAIL: "Namespace mismatch for '<ControlName>'
                          Used:     <used_directive>
                          Expected: <expected_directive>
                          Source:   skill-extraction.json → controls[].using_directive"

  3. VALIDATE every property assigned on this control is in controls[].valid_properties[].name
     ❌ Not found → FAIL: "Property '<propName>' on '<ControlName>' not in skill docs
                           Valid properties: [<list from skill-extraction.json>]
                           Fix: remove the property or re-extract skill file."

  4. VALIDATE every event handler wired on this control is in controls[].valid_events[].name
     ❌ Not found → FAIL: "Event '<eventName>' on '<ControlName>' not in skill docs
                           Valid events: [<list from skill-extraction.json>]"

  5. VALIDATE every method called on this control is in controls[].valid_methods[].name
     ❌ Not found → FAIL: "Method '<methodName>' on '<ControlName>' not verified in skill file"
```

---

### Check 2: WinForms SDK Compliance

For every `Designer.cs` and code-behind `.cs` file, validate all property assignments against the WinForms SDK:

**Framework-level blocked patterns (WPF/WinUI/UWP-origin — not valid in WinForms at all):**

| Property / Pattern | Framework It Belongs To | WinForms Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| `DependencyProperty.Register(...)` | WPF only | Standard CLR property with backing field |
| `{Binding ...}` / `{StaticResource ...}` markup extensions | WPF/XAML only | `DataBindings.Add(...)` or direct property assignment |
| `DataContext = new ViewModel()` | WPF MVVM only | Direct data assignment or Presenter pattern |
| `INotifyPropertyChanged` on Form/Control | WPF pattern | Raise events manually; use `DataBindings` for two-way sync |
| `RoutedEvent` / `AddHandler` / `RemoveHandler` | WPF only | Standard `EventHandler` delegate subscription |
| `UIElement` / `FrameworkElement` base types | WPF only | `Control` / `ContainerControl` / `UserControl` |
| `Windows.UI.*` / `System.Windows.*` types | WinUI/WPF | `System.Windows.Forms.*` / `System.Drawing.*` types |

```
IF any blocked pattern found in generated files
→ FAIL: "Pattern '<name>' is not valid in WinForms (belongs to <framework>)
         File: <file>, Line: <line>
         Fix: <WinForms alternative from table above>"
```

**Control-level property support (examples — not exhaustive):**

The table below shows common violations. The actual rule is broader: **before setting any property on any WinForms control, confirm that property is declared on that control's class (or a base class it inherits from) in the `System.Windows.Forms` SDK.** Do not assume a property exists because it sounds generic.

| Property | Supported On | ❌ NOT Supported On |
|---|---|---|
| `Padding` | `Control` and all subclasses | `Form` title bar area, `ToolStripItem` (use `Margin`) |
| `Dock` | All `Control` subclasses | `ToolStripItem`, `DataGridViewCell` |
| `BackColor` | All `Control` subclasses | `DataGridViewCellStyle` (use `DefaultCellStyle.BackColor`) |
| `Text` | `Control` base class (all subclasses) | `DataGridViewCell` directly (use `Value` or `DefaultCellStyle`) |
| `Items` | `ListBox`, `ComboBox`, `TabControl`, `ListView` | `Panel`, `GroupBox`, `SplitContainer` |
| `SelectedIndex` | `ListBox`, `ComboBox`, `TabControl` | `DataGridView`, `TreeView`, `ListView` (use `SelectedRows` / `SelectedNode` / `SelectedItems`) |
| `Columns` | `DataGridView`, `ListView` (Details mode) | `ListBox`, `ComboBox`, `TreeView` |
| `Nodes` | `TreeView` | `ListBox`, `ComboBox`, `DataGridView` |
| `Checked` | `CheckBox`, `RadioButton`, `CheckedListBox` items | `Button`, `Label`, `Panel` |
| `AutoSize` | `Label`, `Button`, `CheckBox`, `RadioButton` | `Panel`, `GroupBox`, `SplitContainer` (use fixed `Size`) |

**General WinForms compliance rule (MANDATORY — applies to ALL properties, not just the table above):**

```
FOR EACH property assigned on ANY WinForms control in generated Designer.cs or code-behind:

  STEP 1 — Check WinForms SDK class hierarchy:
    Does <ControlType> or any of its base classes declare this property?
    ├── Confirm by tracing: <ControlType> → parent class → ... → Control / Component / object
    ├── Property must appear on one of those classes in System.Windows.Forms
    └── If property is NOT in the class hierarchy → FAIL

  STEP 2 — Check CLR property declaration:
    Is the property a declared CLR property (get/set) on this control type
    in the System.Windows.Forms or System.ComponentModel SDK?
    └── If not declared → FAIL

  STEP 3 — Check value type compatibility:
    Is the assigned value type compatible with the property's declared type?
    Examples:
    ├── BackColor / ForeColor expect System.Drawing.Color — not a raw string like "Red"
    │   (use Color.Red, Color.FromArgb(...), or SystemColors.Control)
    ├── Margin / Padding expect System.Windows.Forms.Padding — not a plain integer
    │   (use new Padding(left, top, right, bottom) or new Padding(uniform))
    ├── Font expects System.Drawing.Font — not a string like "Segoe UI"
    │   (use new Font("Segoe UI", 9F, FontStyle.Regular))
    ├── Size / Location expect System.Drawing.Size / System.Drawing.Point — not plain integers
    │   (use new Size(width, height) or new Point(x, y))
    └── Visible / Enabled expect bool — not a string or integer
    IF type mismatch → FAIL: "Type mismatch: '<property>' on '<ControlType>'
                               Expected: <declared type>
                               Provided: <assigned type>"

  IF any step fails:
  → FAIL: "Property '<propName>' does not exist on '<ControlType>' in WinForms SDK
           File: <file>, Line: <line>
           The System.Windows.Forms type hierarchy does not declare this property
           on <ControlType> or its base classes.
           Fix options:
           - Use the correct container (e.g., TableLayoutPanel for grid layout,
             SplitContainer for resizable panes)
           - Use the correct property for this control type
             (e.g., Items not Nodes on ComboBox)
           - Verify the property name — casing and spelling are exact in C#"
```

---

### Check 3: Designer.cs Structural Validation

Simulate a Designer.cs parse in memory on every generated Designer.cs file before compilation:

```
FOR EACH Designer.cs file:
  Parse structure in memory (dry-run, do not compile)

  Check for:
  ├── Missing partial class declaration
  │   → FAIL: "Designer.cs for '<FormName>' is missing 'partial class <FormName>'
  │            Line: 1. Fix: ensure the class declaration matches the code-behind class name exactly."
  │
  ├── Missing or misplaced InitializeComponent() body
  │   → FAIL: "InitializeComponent() method missing or empty in <file>
  │            All control declarations and property assignments must reside here."
  │
  ├── Missing Dispose() override
  │   → FAIL: "Dispose(bool disposing) override missing in <file>
  │            Fix: add standard Designer Dispose pattern with components?.Dispose()."
  │
  ├── Control variable declared but never added to a container or the Form's Controls collection
  │   → FAIL: "Control '<variableName>' declared in Designer.cs but never added to Controls
  │            Line: <line>. Fix: add this.<container>.Controls.Add(<variableName>)."
  │
  ├── Event subscription referencing a handler name not present in code-behind
  │   → FAIL: "Event subscription '<control>.<event> += <HandlerName>' in Designer.cs
  │            but method '<HandlerName>' not found in <FormName>.cs
  │            Fix: implement the handler in the code-behind file."
  │
  └── Cross-framework namespace import detected (System.Windows.* or Windows.UI.*)
      → FAIL: "Non-WinForms namespace '<ns>' in <file> — mixed framework imports not allowed
               Replace with the equivalent System.Windows.Forms or System.Drawing type."

Auto-fix loop (max 3 attempts):
  IF error is fixable (missing Controls.Add call, missing using directive, mismatched partial name):
    Apply fix → retry parse
  IF cascading errors detected (fix A causes error B causes error A):
    HALT auto-fix → FAIL with cascading error report
  IF 3 attempts exhausted and still failing:
    FAIL: "Designer.cs parse failed after 3 fix attempts — manual review required"
```

---

### Check 4: Runtime Exception Prevention

Detect patterns that compile successfully but throw at runtime:

```
Detect and block:

  InvalidOperationException — SkinManager applied after handle creation:
    ├── Check: SkinManager.SetVisualStyle() / ThemeManager calls occur after
    │          InitializeComponent() but before the Form handle is created
    │          (i.e., not inside a Load event or after Show())
    └── FAIL: "SkinManager theme applied too late in '<FormName>' — will throw
               InvalidOperationException at runtime.
               Fix: apply theme in constructor after InitializeComponent(),
               not in the Load event or any post-show handler."

  NullReferenceException — DataSource assigned before control is initialised:
    ├── Check: DataSource, DataMember, or BindingSource.DataSource is not assigned
    │          before the target control's InitializeComponent() completes
    └── FAIL: "DataSource assigned before control '<controlName>' is initialised
               in '<FormName>' — will throw NullReferenceException at runtime.
               Fix: assign DataSource after InitializeComponent()."

  MissingManifestResourceException — .resx resource key not found:
    ├── Check: every resource key accessed via ResourceManager.GetObject() or
    │          Properties.Resources.<key> resolves to a declared entry in the
    │          corresponding .resx file
    └── FAIL: "Resource key '<key>' not found in '<FormName>.resx'
               — will throw MissingManifestResourceException at runtime.
               Fix: add the missing key/value pair to the .resx file."

  Missing event handler in code-behind:
    ├── Check: every event subscription wired in Designer.cs
    │          (e.g., this.button1.Click += new EventHandler(this.button1_Click))
    │          has a corresponding method with the correct signature in the code-behind file
    └── FAIL: "Event handler '<handlerName>' subscribed in Designer.cs
               but not found in '<FormName>.cs'
               Fix: implement the full handler method — no stubs or empty bodies."
```

---

### Check 5: NuGet Dependency Validation

```
FOR EACH nuget_package in skill-extraction.json → controls[].nuget_package:
  CHECK package is listed in <ProjectName>.csproj → PackageReference
  IF missing:
    → ATTEMPT: dotnet add package <nuget_package> (using resolved version or wildcard)
    → RUN: dotnet restore
    → IF restore fails → FAIL: "Required package '<nuget_package>' could not be installed
                                 Check network, NuGet feed, or package name in skill file"

ALWAYS verify these core packages are present:
  ✅ Syncfusion.Shared.WinForms
  ✅ Syncfusion.Licensing
  ✅ Syncfusion.Tools.WinForms
  ✅ Syncfusion.SfSkinManager.WinForms
  IF any missing → install before build

CHECK all Syncfusion packages use the same version:
  IF version mismatch → FAIL: "Syncfusion version mismatch in .csproj
                                <PackageA>@<versionA> vs <PackageB>@<versionB>
                                All Syncfusion packages must use identical versions"
```

---

### Check 6: Designer.cs & Event Handler Integrity

```
FOR EACH Designer.cs file:
  ├── Every event subscription this.<control>.<event> += <HandlerName>
  │   → method <HandlerName> exists in the paired code-behind file
  │   with the correct delegate signature (e.g., EventHandler, EventHandler<T>)
  │   → FAIL: "Handler '<HandlerName>' subscribed in Designer.cs
  │            but missing or has wrong signature in '<FormName>.cs'"
  │
  ├── InitializeComponent() called exactly once in the Form/UserControl constructor
  │   → FAIL: "InitializeComponent() not called in '<FormName>' constructor
  │            — controls will not be created at runtime"
  │
  └── SkinManager / ThemeManager call present after InitializeComponent()
      and before any data binding or Show() calls
      → FAIL: "SkinManager theme application missing or incorrectly ordered
               in '<FormName>' constructor
               Fix: call SkinManager.SetVisualStyle() immediately after
               InitializeComponent() and before any data binding."

FOR EACH code-behind .cs file:
  ├── No control instantiation or layout code outside InitializeComponent()
  │   → FAIL: "Control instantiation detected outside InitializeComponent() in <file>
  │            Move all control setup to Designer.cs / InitializeComponent()."
  └── No direct visual property assignments (BackColor, Font, Size) in business logic methods
      → FAIL: "Visual property assignment detected in business logic method '<method>'
               in <file> — move to Designer.cs or a dedicated ApplyTheme() method."
```

---

## Build Execution

Run only after all checks above pass:

```bash
dotnet build
```

| Result | Action |
|---|---|
| **0 errors** | ✅ BUILD ALLOWED — proceed to Stage 9 (Code Insertion) |
| **Compile errors** | ❌ Map error to the relevant check above; fix and re-run validation |
| **Warnings only** | ✅ Proceed; log warnings for review |

---

## Error Recovery Reference

| Error / Symptom | Root Check | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `'<Control>' not in skill-extraction.json` | Check 1 | Re-run Stage — Control Skill Extraction for that control |
| `using directive mismatch for <Control>` | Check 1 | Use exact `controls[].using_directive` from skill-extraction.json |
| `Property '<X>' not valid in WinForms` | Check 2 | Replace with WinForms alternative (see Check 2 table) |
| `DependencyProperty.Register found in generated file` | Check 2 | Remove; use standard CLR property with backing field |
| `System.Windows.* namespace imported` | Check 2 | Replace with `System.Windows.Forms.*` or `System.Drawing.*` |
| `Padding / Size / Color type mismatch` | Check 2 | Use `new Padding(...)`, `new Size(...)`, `Color.FromArgb(...)` |
| `partial class declaration missing` | Check 3 | Ensure Designer.cs class name matches code-behind class name exactly |
| `Control declared but not added to Controls` | Check 3 | Add `this.<container>.Controls.Add(<control>)` in Designer.cs |
| `Dispose() override missing` | Check 3 | Add standard Designer `Dispose(bool disposing)` pattern |
| `InvalidOperationException: SkinManager` | Check 4 | Move `SkinManager.SetVisualStyle()` to constructor, after `InitializeComponent()` |
| `NullReferenceException: DataSource` | Check 4 | Assign `DataSource` after `InitializeComponent()` completes |
| `MissingManifestResourceException: '<key>'` | Check 4 | Add missing key/value entry to the corresponding `.resx` file |
| `Required package not installed` | Check 5 | Run `dotnet add package <name>`; verify package name in skill file |
| `Syncfusion version mismatch` | Check 5 | Align all Syncfusion packages to the same version in `.csproj` |
| `Handler missing or wrong signature` | Check 6 | Implement full handler in code-behind with correct `EventHandler` signature |
| `InitializeComponent() not called` | Check 6 | Add `InitializeComponent()` as first statement in constructor |
| `SkinManager call missing or out of order` | Check 6 | Call `SkinManager.SetVisualStyle()` directly after `InitializeComponent()` |
| `Control instantiation outside Designer.cs` | Check 6 | Move all control setup into `Designer.cs` / `InitializeComponent()` |
| Designer.cs parse fails after 3 auto-fix attempts | Check 3 | Return to Stage 5 and regenerate; or manually fix Designer.cs |

---

## Build Gate Summary

```
Check 1: Skill-Based API Validation          ✅ PASS / ❌ FAIL → halt
Check 2: WinForms SDK Compliance             ✅ PASS / ❌ FAIL → halt
Check 3: Designer.cs Structural Validation   ✅ PASS / ❌ FAIL → halt (max 3 auto-fix attempts)
Check 4: Runtime Exception Prevention        ✅ PASS / ❌ FAIL → halt
Check 5: NuGet Dependency Validation         ✅ PASS / ❌ FAIL → halt (auto-install attempted)
Check 6: Designer.cs & Event Handler         ✅ PASS / ❌ FAIL → halt
          ↓
ALL PASS → dotnet build
          ↓
0 errors → ✅ Proceed to Stage 9
```
